title: Gajar ka Halwa: Slow-Cooked Carrot Pudding with Ghee and Cardamom
summary: Grated carrots cooked down in ghee, then simmered in milk with cardamom until thick, sweet and glossy, topped with pistachios and almonds.
equipment: box grater or food processor with grating disc
large heavy-based frying pan or kadai

steps.title: Cook the carrots
steps.text: Melt the ghee in the heavy pan over medium heat and add the grated carrots. Cook for 20-25 min, stirring often, until the liquid they release has evaporated and they look a shade darker and smell sweet. Cooking them dry first deepens the flavour.

steps.title: Simmer with milk
steps.text: Pour in the milk with the crushed cardamom, bring to a lively simmer and cook for 20-25 min, stirring and scraping the base regularly so the milk solids do not catch, until nearly all the milk has been absorbed.

steps.title: Add the sugar
steps.text: Stir in the sugar and keep cooking for 5-8 min. The sugar loosens the mixture at first, then it turns glossy and pulls away from the pan, with a little ghee shining at the edges.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon into bowls while warm and scatter over the pistachio and almond slivers.

tips: Grate the carrots finely for the softest texture; a food processor saves a lot of time.
A common mistake is adding the sugar too early, which keeps the carrots firm.
Use a wide pan so the milk reduces faster.
Juicy, sweet carrots give the best colour and flavour.
storage: Cool, then keep covered in the fridge for up to 4 days or freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat in a pan with a splash of milk.
